guides.title: Configuring Custom Domains for High Availability
guides.desc: Learn how to set up DNS records, SSL certificates, and failover routing for your custom short domains.
guides.content:
Introduction to High Availability Domains

When operating at a global scale, relying on a single DNS endpoint can be a critical point of failure. Setting up custom domains for high availability ensures that your short links always resolve, even during regional outages.

Step 1: Anycast DNS Setup

To achieve minimal latency globally, we strongly recommend using an Anycast DNS provider (like Cloudflare or Route53). This routes your users to the nearest geographical nameserver.

Step 2: Configuring A/AAAA Records

Point your root domain (@) or subdomain to Dragolink's globally load-balanced IP addresses. Ensure you configure both IPv4 (A records) and IPv6 (AAAA records).

Type  Name  Target               TTL
A     link  198.51.100.1        Auto
AAAA  link  2001:db8::1         Auto

SSL Certificate Generation

Dragolink automatically provisions Let's Encrypt wildcard certificates for your domains. However, for enterprise clients requiring custom EV (Extended Validation) certificates, you can upload your .pem and .key files securely via the Dragolink Dashboard under Domains > Security.

Graceful Failover

In the event of an edge node failure, Dragolink's BGP routing will automatically withdraw the failed route, seamlessly redirecting traffic to the next closest POP (Point of Presence) within milliseconds. No manual intervention is required.

guides.title: Automating UTM Tags at Scale
guides.desc: A comprehensive guide to building programmatic UTM builders for your entire marketing team.
guides.content:
The Problem with Manual UTMs

Marketing teams often rely on messy spreadsheets to generate UTM parameters. This leads to inconsistent naming conventions (e.g., source=facebook vs source=FB), which breaks attribution modeling in Google Analytics.

Building a Programmatic Solution

With Dragolink's Link Builder API, you can integrate UTM generation directly into your internal CMS or Slack bots. This ensures every link generated across your organization adheres to a strict schema.

Sample Node.js Implementation

Here's how you can programmatically generate a short link with enforced UTM parameters:

const dragolink = require('dragolink-sdk');

async function createCampaignLink(destination, campaignName) {
  const response = await dragolink.links.create({
    destination: destination,
    utm_source: 'internal_newsletter',
    utm_medium: 'email',
    utm_campaign: campaignName.toLowerCase().replace(/\s+/g, '_')
  });
  
  return response.shortUrl;
}

Best Practices for Tagging

  • Always use lowercase: Email and email are treated as different sources by most analytics platforms.
  • Use underscores instead of spaces: Spaces become %20 in URLs, which makes them ugly and harder to read.
  • Keep it simple: Only use utm_content or utm_term if you are actually running A/B tests or paid search campaigns.

guides.title: Webhooks: Reacting to Link Clicks in Real-Time
guides.desc: Step-by-step tutorial on securing and processing Dragolink webhook payloads in Node.js.
guides.content:
Why Use Webhooks?

While the Dragolink dashboard provides powerful aggregated analytics, sometimes you need to react to individual clicks instantly. For example, triggering an email sequence the moment a user clicks a specific link, or syncing click data into your own Snowflake data warehouse.

Endpoint Configuration

Navigate to Settings > Webhooks in your Dragolink Dashboard. Add your endpoint URL (e.g., https://api.yourcompany.com/webhooks/dragolink). Select the click.created event.

Securing Your Webhook (HMAC)

Dragolink signs all webhook payloads using HMAC-SHA256. It is critical that you verify this signature to ensure the payload actually came from Dragolink and wasn't spoofed.

const crypto = require('crypto');

function verifySignature(payload, signatureHeader, secret) {
  const hash = crypto
    .createHmac('sha256', secret)
    .update(JSON.stringify(payload))
    .digest('hex');
    
  return crypto.timingSafeEqual(
    Buffer.from(hash),
    Buffer.from(signatureHeader)
  );
}

Processing the Payload

The payload contains comprehensive metadata about the click, including geographic location, device type, and referral data. Because Dragolink processes millions of events per second, expect your webhook endpoint to receive high volume. We strongly recommend pushing these payloads into a message queue (like AWS SQS or RabbitMQ) immediately, rather than processing them synchronously.

guides.title: Protecting Users from Phishing and Malware
guides.desc: How Dragolink's automated threat detection works and how to configure custom blocklists.
guides.content:
The Threat Landscape

URL shorteners are frequently abused by bad actors to hide malicious destinations. If your custom domain is used to serve malware, it will be flagged by Google Safe Browsing, destroying your email deliverability and brand reputation.

Dragolink's Automated Shield

Dragolink automatically scans every destination URL created on our platform against multiple global threat intelligence databases (including Google Safe Browsing, SURBL, and PhishTank).

If a destination URL is flagged:

  1. The link creation is instantly blocked.
  2. If an existing link's destination becomes malicious later, it is automatically suspended and redirects to a warning page.

Configuring Custom Blocklists

Enterprise administrators can enforce strict URL policies. Navigate to Security > Policies to configure:

  • Allowed Domains (Allowlist): Only allow links pointing to your own web properties (e.g., *.yourcompany.com). This completely eliminates the risk of abuse.
  • Banned Keywords: Prevent links that contain certain high-risk keywords in their destination paths.
  • Geographic Restrictions: Block traffic originating from specific high-risk countries from accessing your links.

Auditing and Alerts

Set up instant Slack or Email alerts for whenever a team member attempts to create a link to a flagged domain. Regular security audits of your link infrastructure are essential for maintaining domain health.
